scope_entries.finding: ranking tests are hermetic by construction - EmbedClient(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:1/v1") forces the local fallback, and test_scoring.py injects a fake client whose embed_detect reports online=True to exercise the blend without a server. test_embed.py already covers rerank() determinism against a dead port, i.e. the fallback path only.

scope_entries.surface: docs/contract.md §5 + tests/test_embed_default_drift.py + both vendored wrappers
scope_entries.finding: a three-surface drift lock already binds embed_default_url/model/rerank_model across the contract block, the embed.py constants and the := exports in recall.sh and remember.sh. EIDETIC_RERANK_MODEL is already in all three; a new EIDETIC_RERANK env default would have to join them or CI fails.

scope_entries.surface: .claude/skills/recall/{SKILL.md,scripts/recall.sh}
scope_entries.finding: recall.sh ends in exec ... recall "${SCOPE_ARGS[@]}" "$@", forwarding every flag verbatim - so --rerank needs no wrapper code change. Only the enumerated flag lists drift: the usage() heredoc, the SKILL.md frontmatter description and its mode table. These wrappers are fanned out to ~57 org repos.

scope_entries.surface: the hand-maintained docs trio + README (explain/catalog.py _RECALL, learn.py _TEXT/_as_json_payload, overview.py _VERBS)
scope_entries.finding: CLAUDE.md names these three as the surface that drifts if one is forgotten; catalog.py _RECALL is the long verbatim recall doc (~150 lines) covering modes, tiers, bounds and reinforcement, and README.md line 40 restates the whole flag list a fourth time.

scope_entries.surface: issue #3 (jetson-ai-lab-cli) + issue #1 (research flow) consumer contracts
scope_entries.finding: both are named in CLAUDE.md as the authoritative consumer contracts, and #3 requires mandatory provenance (text + full metadata + score) on every hit. Adding rerank_score is additive and safe for them; silently reordering the primary tier is not, which is what forces opt-in. 0.13.0 already spent one breaking bundle change on these consumers.

scope_entries.surface: lobes-cli #227 / #220 and docs/qwen3-reranker-0.6b.md calibration notes
scope_entries.finding: the untemplated-scoring bug is fixed upstream and measured; the residual conditions are lobes-side - score saturation at 1.000 on short graded pairs, and Thor/Orin serving untemplated scores until their next `lobes init --apply`. eidetic reports these, it does not fix them.

scope_entries.surface: CLAUDE.md non-negotiable workflow rules
scope_entries.finding: every PR bumps the version (version-check CI job compares against main) and `teken cli doctor . --strict` gates the agent-first rubric - a new flag must keep explain/learn/overview coherent or the rubric fails. Lint set is black/isort/flake8/bandit plus markdownlint.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / missing-counter-evidence lens: live lobes lane, multi-relevant-doc probe
scope_entries.finding: the frame assumed the lane is graded because the issue measured one query where the gap was total (0.993/0.936 vs 0.000). Probed the opposite case - four genuinely on-topic docs - and the lane is near-binary: 0.9998/0.9963 for direct answers, 0.0048/0.0035 for topically-relevant supporting records, against a 1.7e-4 irrelevant floor. Nobody had argued the other side.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / failure-mode lens: eidetic/memory/embed.py _remote_rerank score_map
scope_entries.finding: score_map.get(i, 0.0) defaults any index the server omits to 0.0. Benign as a ranking input; under a threshold it is a silent drop, so a partial response deletes records from recall with no error.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / adjacent-systems lens: eidetic/memory/backend.py record_to_envelope + record_from_envelope
scope_entries.finding: persistence is an explicit field whitelist, not a null-then-dump - score/signal are omitted by construction. rerank_score therefore cannot persist regardless of cmd_recall, which makes the obvious round-trip test vacuous. Third occurrence of this trap in this repo.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / adjacent-systems lens: ../colleague/colleague/memory.py filter_recall_records + score_recall_precision
scope_entries.finding: a sibling consumer ALREADY thresholds recall output on score/signal (COLLEAGUE_RECALL_MIN_SCORE) and ranks over the recalled order - so eidetic reordering by rerank_score while leaving score at its hybrid value makes that consumer cut the reranker top hits. Discovered by reading the consumer, not inferred.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / observability lens: issue #37 never-a-silent-cut precedent in recall.py
scope_entries.finding: the bundle already reports truncated when a traversal bound cuts the walk. A relevance threshold dropping primary hits is the same class of cut with no marker - the precedent exists in-repo and the frame had not applied it.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / security lens: embed.py key resolution + _may_send_key + the pool widening
scope_entries.finding: record text crosses the HTTP boundary and the pool multiplies private text volume ~10x per call; and the fail-closed remediation must name key VARIABLES, never interpolate a resolved key value into stderr.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / cost-and-operations lens: timed 5-doc and 50-doc probes against the live gateway
scope_entries.finding: measured rather than assumed: 50 docs = 5677 prompt tokens, one request, all 50 results, 0.07s (5 docs: 0.04s). Counter-evidence against my own suspicion that the wider pool was expensive; the loaded-fleet-under-concurrency case remains unmeasured.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / reversibility + migration lens: the opt-in flag surface
scope_entries.finding: CLEAN pass, with a stated reason: --rerank is opt-in and adds no stored state (the envelope whitelist forbids it), so backing the feature out is deleting a flag - no store migration, no downgrade path, no data to unwind. Residual risk only if a later change makes rerank_score persistent.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / concurrency lens: recall reinforcement upsert path
scope_entries.finding: CLEAN pass, no NEW hazard: recall already upserts reinforcement bumps with no locking and concurrent recalls can already interleave writes. The threshold changes WHICH records get bumped but adds no new write, so the pre-existing race is unchanged - explicitly not introduced by this work, and explicitly not fixed by it either.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / overlooked-actors lens: the ~57 fanned-out wrapper repos and the mesh agents sharing the store
scope_entries.finding: NOT fully examined, and stating why: the flag is opt-in and forwards verbatim, so no fanned-out wrapper changes behaviour until someone passes --rerank. I read the local recall.sh and colleague/memory.py but did NOT survey the other consumers of recall output across the org - if another one thresholds or re-sorts on score like colleague does, c37 applies to it too and this pass would not have found it.
